subproblems.title: Directional difference estimate from the divergence bound (parent step 2)
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let (X, ν) be a finite measure space, let q : X → ℝⁿ (Euclid n) be measurable, h : X → ℝ ν-integrable, and Λ ∈ ℝ. Assume |∫ h(x)·div g(q(x)) dν(x)| ≤ Λ for every C^∞ map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support and ‖g(y)‖ ≤ 1 for all y, where div g(y) := LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid n) (fderiv ℝ g y). Then for every C^∞ function a : ℝⁿ → ℝ with compact support and |a(y)| ≤ 1 for all y, and every z ∈ ℝⁿ, |∫ h(x)·(a(q(x) + z) − a(q(x))) dν(x)| ≤ Λ‖z‖.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (X : Type) [MeasurableSpace X] (ν : Measure X) (q : X → Euclid n) (h : X → ℝ) (Λ : ℝ), IsFiniteMeasure ν → Measurable q → Integrable h ν → (∀ g : Euclid n → Euclid n, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g → HasCompactSupport g → (∀ y, ‖g y‖ ≤ 1) → |∫ x, h x * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid n) (fderiv ℝ g (q x)).toLinearMap ∂ν| ≤ Λ) → ∀ a : Euclid n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) a → HasCompactSupport a → (∀ y, |a y| ≤ 1) → ∀ z : Euclid n, |∫ x, h x * (a (q x + z) - a (q x)) ∂ν| ≤ Λ * ‖z‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 2 (directional estimate), with the derivative, measurability and integrability details written out. Parent step 1 (Λ ≥ 0) is not used, and the argument never uses the sign of Λ.
Notation: for y ∈ ℝⁿ, Da(y) := fderiv ℝ a y, a continuous linear functional on ℝⁿ. For g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ, div g(y) := LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid n) (fderiv ℝ g y). Fix a C^∞ function a : ℝⁿ → ℝ with compact support and |a| ≤ 1, and fix z ∈ ℝⁿ.
1. (Regularity of a.) The smoothness order ∞ is ≥ 1. So a is differentiable everywhere (ContDiff.differentiable), and Da : ℝⁿ → L(ℝⁿ, ℝ) is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv). Since a has compact support, so does Da (HasCompactSupport.fderiv). A continuous function with compact support is bounded (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support), so there is M with ‖Da(y)‖ ≤ M for all y.
2. (Case z = 0.) Then a(q x + z) − a(q x) = 0 for every x, so the integral is 0 and |0| = 0 = Λ·‖0‖. From now on assume z ≠ 0 and put w := ‖z‖⁻¹•z. Then ‖w‖ = 1 and z = ‖z‖•w.
3. (Admissible fields.) Fix s ∈ ℝ and define g_s : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ by g_s(y) := a(y + s•z)•w.
 (a) g_s is C^∞. The map y ↦ y + s•z is C^∞ and a is C^∞, so y ↦ a(y + s•z) is C^∞ (ContDiff.comp). Multiplying a C^∞ real function by the fixed vector w gives a C^∞ map (ContDiff.smul with contDiff_const).
 (b) g_s has compact support. The map y ↦ a(y + s•z) equals a ∘ τ for the homeomorphism τ = Homeomorph.addRight (s•z), so it has compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph). Multiplying by the constant w preserves this (HasCompactSupport.smul_right).
 (c) ‖g_s(y)‖ = |a(y + s•z)|·‖w‖ = |a(y + s•z)| ≤ 1 for every y.
 (d) By the chain rule for a translation (hasFDerivAt_comp_add_right), y ↦ a(y + s•z) has derivative Da(y + s•z) at y. By HasFDerivAt.smul_const, g_s has derivative Da(y + s•z).smulRight w at y. This is the linear map v ↦ Da(y + s•z)(v)•w. Hence fderiv ℝ g_s y = Da(y + s•z).smulRight w (HasFDerivAt.fderiv). Its underlying linear map is ℓ.smulRight w, where ℓ is Da(y + s•z) viewed as a linear map (ContinuousLinearMap.coe_smulRight). Euclid n is free and finite-dimensional, so the trace of ℓ.smulRight w is ℓ(w) (LinearMap.trace_smulRight). Hence div g_s(y) = Da(y + s•z)(w).
 (e) Apply the hypothesis to g = g_s and use (d) at y = q x. For every s ∈ ℝ,
   |∫ h(x)·Da(q x + s•z)(w) dν(x)| ≤ Λ.   (∗)
4. (Fundamental theorem of calculus.) Fix x ∈ X and let φ(s) := a(q x + s•z).
 - The curve s ↦ q x + s•z has derivative z at every s. By the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt), φ has derivative Da(q x + s•z)(z) at every s ∈ ℝ.
 - The map s ↦ Da(q x + s•z)(z) is continuous, since Da is continuous and evaluation at z is continuous. Hence it is interval integrable on [0, 1].
 - By intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt,
   a(q x + z) − a(q x) = φ(1) − φ(0) = ∫_0^1 Da(q x + s•z)(z) ds.
 - Multiplying by the constant h(x) (intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul) gives
   h(x)·(a(q x + z) − a(q x)) = ∫_0^1 h(x)·Da(q x + s•z)(z) ds.
5. (Fubini.) Let μ₁ be Lebesgue measure on ℝ restricted to uIoc 0 1 = Ioc 0 1. It is a finite measure, and ∫_0^1 f(s) ds = ∫ f dμ₁. Since ν is finite, it is s-finite. On ℝ × X, with the product measure μ₁ ⊗ ν, define G(s, x) := h(x)·Da(q x + s•z)(z).
 (a) G is AE-strongly measurable for μ₁ ⊗ ν.
 - The map (s, x) ↦ h(x) is AE-strongly measurable, because h is AE-strongly measurable for ν (AEStronglyMeasurable.snd).
 - The map (s, x) ↦ Da(q x + s•z)(z) is measurable: it is the continuous map (s, y) ↦ Da(y + s•z)(z) composed with the measurable map (s, x) ↦ (s, q x).
 - The product of the two is AE-strongly measurable.
 (b) G is μ₁ ⊗ ν-integrable.
 - |G(s, x)| ≤ |h(x)|·‖Da(q x + s•z)‖·‖z‖ ≤ M‖z‖·|h(x)|, by ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm and step 1.
 - The map (s, x) ↦ 1·|h(x)| is μ₁ ⊗ ν-integrable (Integrable.mul_prod): the constant 1 is μ₁-integrable since μ₁ is finite, and |h| is ν-integrable.
 - So the majorant (s, x) ↦ M‖z‖·|h(x)| is integrable, and G ∈ L¹(μ₁ ⊗ ν) (Integrable.mono').
 (c) Integrate the identity of step 4, which holds for every x. Then apply Fubini for interval integrals (intervalIntegral_integral_swap, applied to G):
   ∫ h(x)(a(q x + z) − a(q x)) dν(x) = ∫ (∫_0^1 G(s, x) ds) dν(x) = ∫_0^1 Φ(s) ds,
 where Φ(s) := ∫ h(x)·Da(q x + s•z)(z) dν(x).
6. (Bound.) Each Da(p) is linear and z = ‖z‖•w, so Da(p)(z) = ‖z‖·Da(p)(w).
 - Hence Φ(s) = ‖z‖·∫ h(x)·Da(q x + s•z)(w) dν(x) (integral_const_mul).
 - By (∗), |Φ(s)| ≤ ‖z‖·Λ = Λ‖z‖ for every s ∈ ℝ.
 - By intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const, |∫_0^1 Φ(s) ds| ≤ Λ‖z‖·|1 − 0| = Λ‖z‖.
 By step 5(c), this is the claim |∫ h(x)(a(q x + z) − a(q x)) dν(x)| ≤ Λ‖z‖.
proof_key_steps: Da is continuous with compact support, so ‖Da‖ ≤ M. The case z = 0 is trivial; otherwise put w := z/‖z‖.
g_s(y) := a(y + s•z)•w is C^∞, has compact support and satisfies ‖g_s‖ ≤ 1. By the rank-one trace, div g_s(y) = Da(y + s•z)(w), so |∫ h(x)·Da(q x + s•z)(w) dν| ≤ Λ for every s.
FTC: h(x)(a(q x + z) − a(q x)) = ∫_0^1 h(x)·Da(q x + s•z)(z) ds.
Fubini on Leb|(0,1] ⊗ ν, with integrable majorant M‖z‖|h(x)|, gives ∫ h(a(q+z) − a(q)) dν = ∫_0^1 Φ(s) ds, where Φ(s) = ∫ h(x)·Da(q x + s•z)(z) dν.
Da(·)(z) = ‖z‖·Da(·)(w) gives |Φ(s)| ≤ Λ‖z‖. The constant bound on [0, 1] gives the claim.

subproblems.title: Ball-averaging estimate for test functions (parent step 3)
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let (X, ν) be a finite measure space, let q : X → ℝⁿ (Euclid n) be measurable, h : X → ℝ ν-integrable, Λ ≥ 0, a : ℝⁿ → ℝ continuous (smoothness is not required) with compact support and 0 ≤ a(y) ≤ 1 for all y, and r > 0. Assume |∫ h(x)·(a(q(x) + z) − a(q(x))) dν(x)| ≤ Λ‖z‖ for every z ∈ ℝⁿ. Then |∫ h(x)·a(q(x)) dν(x)| ≤ r·Λ + (λ(ball(0, r)).toReal)⁻¹·(∫ |h| dν)·∫ a dλ, where λ is Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝⁿ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (X : Type) [MeasurableSpace X] (ν : Measure X) (q : X → Euclid n) (h : X → ℝ) (Λ : ℝ) (a : Euclid n → ℝ) (r : ℝ), IsFiniteMeasure ν → Measurable q → Integrable h ν → 0 ≤ Λ → Continuous a → HasCompactSupport a → (∀ y, 0 ≤ a y) → (∀ y, a y ≤ 1) → (∀ z : Euclid n, |∫ x, h x * (a (q x + z) - a (q x)) ∂ν| ≤ Λ * ‖z‖) → 0 < r → |∫ x, h x * a (q x) ∂ν| ≤ r * Λ + (volume (ball (0 : Euclid n) r)).toReal⁻¹ * (∫ x, |h x| ∂ν) * ∫ y, a y
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 3 (averaging estimate), with the Fubini and translation-invariance details written out. The parent's step-2 directional estimate is a hypothesis here, and so is Λ ≥ 0 (parent step 1). Only continuity of a is used, not smoothness.
Notation: λ := volume on ℝⁿ = Euclid n. It is an additive Haar measure: translation invariant, σ-finite, finite on compact sets and positive on nonempty open sets. Write B := ball(0, r), V := λ(B).toReal, c := V⁻¹, ‖h‖₁ := ∫|h| dν, A := ∫ a dλ and F := ∫ h(x)a(q x) dν(x).
1. (The ball.) B is open and nonempty since r > 0, so λ(B) > 0 (measure_ball_pos). B is bounded in the proper space ℝⁿ, so λ(B) < ∞ (measure_ball_lt_top). Hence V > 0 (ENNReal.toReal_pos), c > 0 and V·c = 1.
2. (Basic integrability.)
 - a is continuous with compact support, so it is λ-integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport).
 - Let ψ := c·1_B, the indicator of B with value c. Then ψ is measurable. It is λ-integrable because B is measurable with λ(B) < ∞ (integrableOn_const, then IntegrableOn.integrable_indicator).
 - Also 0 ≤ ψ ≤ c and ψ = 0 off B. Moreover ∫ψ dλ = λ(B).toReal·c = V·c = 1 (integral_indicator_const, measureReal_def).
 - For every p ∈ ℝⁿ, z ↦ a(p + z) is λ-integrable (Integrable.comp_add_left). By translation invariance of λ, ∫ a(p + z) dλ(z) = A (integral_add_left_eq_self).
3. (Product integrands.) Give X × ℝⁿ the product measure ν ⊗ λ; ν is finite and λ is σ-finite, so both are s-finite. Define
   G₁(x, z) := h(x)·ψ(z)·(a(q x) − a(q x + z)),   G₂(x, z) := h(x)·ψ(z)·a(q x + z).
 (a) Both are AE-strongly measurable:
 - (x, z) ↦ h(x) is AE-strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.fst);
 - (x, z) ↦ ψ(z) is measurable;
 - (x, z) ↦ a(q x) and (x, z) ↦ a(q x + z) are the continuous function a composed with the measurable maps (x, z) ↦ q x and (x, z) ↦ q x + z (addition on ℝⁿ is measurable).
 (b) Both are integrable. Since 0 ≤ a ≤ 1, |a(u) − a(v)| ≤ 1 and |a(u)| ≤ 1 for all u, v. Hence |G₁(x, z)| ≤ |h(x)|ψ(z) and |G₂(x, z)| ≤ |h(x)|ψ(z). The map (x, z) ↦ |h(x)|ψ(z) is ν ⊗ λ-integrable (Integrable.mul_prod, with |h| ∈ L¹(ν) and ψ ∈ L¹(λ)). Hence G₁, G₂ ∈ L¹(ν ⊗ λ) (Integrable.mono').
 (c) Consequences of Fubini. The maps x ↦ ∫ G₁(x, z) dλ(z) and x ↦ ∫ G₂(x, z) dλ(z) are ν-integrable (Integrable.integral_prod_left). For ν-a.e. x, the slices z ↦ G₁(x, z) and z ↦ G₂(x, z) are λ-integrable (Integrable.prod_right_ae).
4. (Splitting F.) For all x and z, G₁(x, z) + G₂(x, z) = h(x)a(q x)·ψ(z).
 - For each x whose two slices are integrable (ν-a.e. x), ∫ G₁(x, z) dλ(z) + ∫ G₂(x, z) dλ(z) = h(x)a(q x)·∫ψ dλ = h(x)a(q x) (integral_add, integral_const_mul).
 - Integrate this ν-a.e. identity in x (integral_congr_ae, then integral_add with the integrability from step 3).
 This gives F = F₁ + F₂, where F_i := ∫ (∫ G_i(x, z) dλ(z)) dν(x).
5. (Bound on F₁.) By Fubini (integral_integral_swap for G₁ ∈ L¹(ν ⊗ λ)),
   F₁ = ∫ (∫ G₁(x, z) dν(x)) dλ(z) = ∫ ψ(z)·J(z) dλ(z),
 where J(z) := ∫ h(x)(a(q x) − a(q x + z)) dν(x) = −∫ h(x)(a(q x + z) − a(q x)) dν(x) (integral_const_mul, integral_neg). By hypothesis, |J(z)| ≤ Λ‖z‖.
 - If z ∈ B, then ‖z‖ < r. Since Λ ≥ 0 and ψ ≥ 0, |ψ(z)J(z)| = ψ(z)|J(z)| ≤ ψ(z)Λ‖z‖ ≤ ψ(z)Λr.
 - If z ∉ B, then ψ(z)J(z) = 0 = ψ(z)Λr.
 The function z ↦ ψ(z)Λr is integrable, so |F₁| ≤ ∫ ψ(z)Λr dλ(z) = Λr (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le, integral_mul_const).
6. (Bound on F₂.) For each x, ∫ G₂(x, z) dλ(z) = h(x)·m(x), where m(x) := ∫ ψ(z)a(q x + z) dλ(z) (integral_const_mul).
 - We have 0 ≤ ψ(z)a(q x + z) ≤ c·a(q x + z), and z ↦ c·a(q x + z) is integrable (step 2).
 - So 0 ≤ m(x) (integral_nonneg). Also m(x) ≤ ∫ c·a(q x + z) dλ(z) = c·A, by integral_mono_of_nonneg, integral_const_mul and step 2.
 - Therefore |h(x)m(x)| ≤ |h(x)|·cA, and |F₂| ≤ ∫ |h(x)|·cA dν(x) = ‖h‖₁·cA (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le, integral_mul_const).
7. (Conclusion.) |F| ≤ |F₁| + |F₂| ≤ Λr + ‖h‖₁·cA = r·Λ + c·‖h‖₁·A. That is,
   |∫ h(x)a(q x) dν(x)| ≤ r·Λ + (λ(B).toReal)⁻¹·(∫|h| dν)·∫ a dλ.
proof_key_steps: 0 < λ(B_r) < ∞. ψ := λ(B_r).toReal⁻¹·1_{B_r} satisfies 0 ≤ ψ ≤ λ(B_r).toReal⁻¹ and ∫ψ dλ = 1. By translation invariance, ∫ a(p + z) dλ(z) = ∫ a dλ.
G₁ = h(x)ψ(z)(a(q x) − a(q x + z)) and G₂ = h(x)ψ(z)a(q x + z) are ν ⊗ λ-integrable, with majorant |h(x)|ψ(z). Since ∫ψ = 1, F = F₁ + F₂.
By Fubini, F₁ = ∫ψ(z)J(z) dλ, and |J(z)| ≤ Λ‖z‖ ≤ Λr on B_r, so |F₁| ≤ rΛ.
By translation invariance, 0 ≤ ∫ψ(z)a(q x + z) dλ(z) ≤ λ(B_r).toReal⁻¹∫a, so |F₂| ≤ λ(B_r).toReal⁻¹‖h‖₁∫a.

subproblems.title: Smooth cut-offs of a compact Lebesgue-null set (parent steps 4 and 5(ii))
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ and let K ⊆ ℝⁿ (Euclid n) be compact with Lebesgue measure λ(K) = 0. Then there are functions a_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) such that: each a_k is C^∞ with compact support and 0 ≤ a_k ≤ 1; a_k = 1 on K for every k; for every y ∉ K, a_k(y) = 0 for all sufficiently large k; and ∫ a_k dλ → 0 as k → ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (K : Set (Euclid n)), IsCompact K → volume K = 0 → ∃ a : ℕ → Euclid n → ℝ, (∀ k, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (a k)) ∧ (∀ k, HasCompactSupport (a k)) ∧ (∀ k y, 0 ≤ a k y) ∧ (∀ k y, a k y ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ k, ∀ y ∈ K, a k y = 1) ∧ (∀ y, y ∉ K → ∀ᶠ k in atTop, a k y = 0) ∧ Tendsto (fun k => ∫ y, a k y) atTop (𝓝 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 4 (cut-offs), together with the parts of step 5 that concern only the cut-offs: pointwise convergence to 1_K (from 5(i)) and ∫ a_k → λ(K) = 0 (5(ii)). The radii are uniform, ρ_k = 1/(3(k+1)). This is a valid choice of the parent's ρ_x for O_k = thickening(1/(k+1)) K, since closedBall(x, 2ρ_k) ⊆ O_k for x ∈ K.
Notation: λ := volume on ℝⁿ = Euclid n. For k ∈ ℕ, put δ_k := 1/(k+1) > 0 and ρ_k := δ_k/3 > 0.
1. (Finite covers.) Fix k. Since K is compact, there is a finite set T_k ⊆ K with K ⊆ ⋃_{p ∈ T_k} ball(p, ρ_k) (IsCompact.finite_cover_balls). Choose such a T_k for every k, and regard it as a Finset. If K = ∅, then T_k = ∅.
2. (Bumps.) Euclid n has a HasContDiffBump instance. For p ∈ ℝⁿ, let φ_{k,p} be the smooth bump function (a term of ContDiffBump p) centred at p, with inner radius rIn = ρ_k and outer radius rOut = 2ρ_k. This is valid since 0 < ρ_k < 2ρ_k. Its properties:
 - φ_{k,p} is C^∞ (ContDiffBump.contDiff);
 - 0 ≤ φ_{k,p} ≤ 1 (ContDiffBump.nonneg, ContDiffBump.le_one);
 - φ_{k,p}(y) = 1 for y ∈ closedBall(p, ρ_k) (ContDiffBump.one_of_mem_closedBall);
 - φ_{k,p}(y) = 0 whenever dist(y, p) ≥ 2ρ_k (ContDiffBump.zero_of_le_dist).
3. (Definition.) a_k(y) := 1 − P_k(y), where P_k(y) := ∏_{p ∈ T_k} (1 − φ_{k,p}(y)).
4. (Smoothness and range.) Each factor y ↦ 1 − φ_{k,p}(y) is C^∞, and a finite product of C^∞ functions is C^∞ (contDiff_prod). So a_k is C^∞. For every y, each factor lies in [0, 1], so 0 ≤ P_k(y) ≤ 1 (Finset.prod_nonneg, Finset.prod_le_one₀). Hence a_k(y) = 1 − P_k(y) ∈ [0, 1].
5. (a_k = 1 on K.) Let y ∈ K. By step 1, y ∈ ball(p, ρ_k) ⊆ closedBall(p, ρ_k) for some p ∈ T_k. Then φ_{k,p}(y) = 1, so the factor 1 − φ_{k,p}(y) vanishes. Hence P_k(y) = 0 (Finset.prod_eq_zero) and a_k(y) = 1.
6. (Support.) Let y ∉ cthickening(δ_k) K and p ∈ T_k.
 - Since p ∈ K, dist(y, p) ≤ δ_k would put y in cthickening(δ_k) K (Metric.mem_cthickening_of_dist_le). So dist(y, p) > δ_k = 3ρ_k ≥ 2ρ_k, and φ_{k,p}(y) = 0.
 - Hence every factor equals 1, so P_k(y) = 1 (Finset.prod_eq_one) and a_k(y) = 0.
 Thus a_k vanishes outside cthickening(δ_k) K. That set is compact (IsCompact.cthickening, ℝⁿ being proper), so a_k has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro).
7. (Eventual vanishing off K.) Let y ∉ K.
 - K is compact, hence closed, so K = closure K = ⋂_{δ>0} cthickening(δ) K (Metric.closure_eq_iInter_cthickening). Hence there is δ > 0 with y ∉ cthickening(δ) K.
 - Choose k₀ ∈ ℕ with 1/(k₀+1) < δ (exists_nat_one_div_lt). For k ≥ k₀, δ_k = 1/(k+1) ≤ 1/(k₀+1) < δ (one_div_le_one_div_of_le).
 - So cthickening(δ_k) K ⊆ cthickening(δ) K (Metric.cthickening_mono), and this set does not contain y.
 By step 6, a_k(y) = 0 for all k ≥ k₀.
8. (Integrals.) Let C_k := cthickening(δ_k) K. It is closed, hence measurable, and compact, hence λ(C_k) < ∞ (IsCompact.measure_lt_top).
 - By steps 4 and 6, 0 ≤ a_k ≤ 1_{C_k} pointwise, and 1_{C_k} is integrable (integrableOn_const, IntegrableOn.integrable_indicator).
 - Hence 0 ≤ ∫ a_k dλ (integral_nonneg), and ∫ a_k dλ ≤ ∫ 1_{C_k} dλ = λ(C_k).toReal (integral_mono_of_nonneg, integral_indicator_const, measureReal_def).
 - λ is finite on compact sets, so by tendsto_measure_cthickening_of_isCompact, λ(cthickening(δ) K) → λ(K) = 0 as δ → 0.
 - Since δ_k → 0 (tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat), λ(C_k) → 0 in [0, ∞]. Then λ(C_k).toReal → 0, since ENNReal.toReal is continuous at the finite value 0 (ENNReal.tendsto_toReal).
 By the squeeze theorem (tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le), ∫ a_k dλ → 0.
9. (Conclusion.) The family (a_k) has every required property:
 - C^∞ (step 4);
 - compact support (step 6);
 - 0 ≤ a_k ≤ 1 (step 4);
 - a_k = 1 on K (step 5);
 - eventual vanishing at each y ∉ K (step 7);
 - ∫ a_k dλ → 0 (step 8).
 No case distinction is needed: if K = ∅, then T_k = ∅, P_k = 1 and a_k = 0. Dimension n = 0 is not special.
Remark (equivalent shortcut for steps 1–6). exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff is in the import closure. Apply it, with smoothness order ⊤, to the open set thickening(δ_k) K and the closed set K ⊆ thickening(δ_k) K (self_subset_thickening). It directly gives a C^∞ function a_k with range in [0, 1], support a_k = thickening(δ_k) K ⊆ cthickening(δ_k) K (thickening_subset_cthickening), and a_k(y) = 1 exactly for y ∈ K. The compact-support argument of step 6 and steps 7–9 then apply unchanged.
proof_key_steps: Cover K by finitely many balls ball(p, ρ_k), p ∈ T_k ⊆ K, with ρ_k = 1/(3(k+1)).
Put a_k := 1 − ∏_{p∈T_k}(1 − φ_{k,p}), where φ_{k,p} is a ContDiffBump with radii ρ_k and 2ρ_k. Then a_k is C^∞, takes values in [0, 1] and equals 1 on K.
a_k = 0 off cthickening(1/(k+1)) K, which is compact, so a_k has compact support.
If y ∉ K, then y ∉ cthickening(δ) K for some δ > 0, so a_k(y) = 0 for all large k.

subproblems.title: Vanishing on compact null sets from an ε + C∫a bound (parent steps 5(i) and 6)
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let (X, ν) be a measure space (ν need not be finite), let q : X → ℝⁿ (Euclid n) be measurable and h : X → ℝ ν-integrable. Assume that for every ε > 0 there is C ∈ ℝ such that, for every C^∞ function a : ℝⁿ → ℝ with compact support and 0 ≤ a ≤ 1, |∫ h(x)·a(q(x)) dν(x)| ≤ ε + C·∫ a dλ, where λ is Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝⁿ. Then ∫_{q⁻¹(K)} h dν = 0 for every compact K ⊆ ℝⁿ with λ(K) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (X : Type) [MeasurableSpace X] (ν : Measure X) (q : X → Euclid n) (h : X → ℝ), Measurable q → Integrable h ν → (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ a : Euclid n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) a → HasCompactSupport a → (∀ y, 0 ≤ a y) → (∀ y, a y ≤ 1) → |∫ x, h x * a (q x) ∂ν| ≤ ε + C * ∫ y, a y) → ∀ K : Set (Euclid n), IsCompact K → volume K = 0 → ∫ x in q ⁻¹' K, h x ∂ν = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 5(i) and 6 (dominated convergence along smooth cut-offs, then the error term tends to 0). The parent's step-3 bound rΛ + λ(B_r)⁻¹‖h‖₁∫a is abstracted to ε + C∫a. The cut-offs come from the sibling lemma cmr_tdn_null_set_cutoffs (key null_set_cutoffs). Finiteness of ν is not needed.
Notation: λ := volume on ℝⁿ = Euclid n, and F(a) := ∫ h(x)a(q x) dν(x).
1. (Cut-offs.) Fix a compact K with λ(K) = 0. The sibling lemma cmr_tdn_null_set_cutoffs, applied to n and K, gives functions a_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) with these properties:
 - each a_k is C^∞ with compact support and 0 ≤ a_k ≤ 1;
 - a_k = 1 on K for every k;
 - for every y ∉ K, a_k(y) = 0 for all large k;
 - ∫ a_k dλ → 0.
2. (The target integral.) K is compact in the Hausdorff space ℝⁿ, hence closed and Borel. Since q is measurable, E := q⁻¹(K) is measurable. Put I := ∫_E h dν. By integral_indicator, I = ∫ 1_E(x)h(x) dν(x).
3. (Dominated convergence.) Let F_k(x) := h(x)a_k(q x).
 - Each F_k is AE-strongly measurable: h is, and a_k ∘ q is measurable because a_k is continuous (being C^∞) and q is measurable.
 - Since 0 ≤ a_k ≤ 1, |F_k(x)| ≤ |h(x)| for every x, and |h| is ν-integrable.
 - Pointwise convergence: if q x ∈ K, then F_k(x) = h(x) = 1_E(x)h(x) for every k. If q x ∉ K, then F_k(x) = 0 = 1_E(x)h(x) for all large k. Hence F_k(x) → 1_E(x)h(x) for every x.
 By dominated convergence (tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence with bound |h|), F(a_k) = ∫ F_k dν → I.
4. (ε-bound.) Fix ε > 0 and let C be given by the hypothesis.
 - Every a_k is admissible, so |F(a_k)| ≤ ε + C∫ a_k dλ for every k.
 - As k → ∞, the left side tends to |I| (continuity of |·|, Tendsto.abs), and the right side tends to ε + C·0 = ε, whatever the sign of C.
 - Limits preserve non-strict inequalities (le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto'), so |I| ≤ ε.
5. (Conclusion.) |I| ≤ 0 + ε for every ε > 0, so |I| ≤ 0 (le_of_forall_pos_le_add). Hence |I| = 0 (abs_nonpos_iff), and ∫_{q⁻¹(K)} h dν = I = 0.
proof_key_steps: Take the cut-offs a_k of K from the sibling lemma cmr_tdn_null_set_cutoffs.
q⁻¹(K) is measurable. Dominated convergence with majorant |h| gives F(a_k) → ∫_{q⁻¹(K)} h dν.
For each ε > 0, |F(a_k)| ≤ ε + C∫a_k → ε, so |∫_{q⁻¹(K)} h dν| ≤ ε.
Since ε > 0 is arbitrary, the integral is 0.
